neighbours.label: ' to' after a motion verb, introducing the destination (went to | work, going to | the park); the + pole is the other side of the direction: 'out / away'
fire: Last summer my cousins drove to the coast for a week.
When the storm hit, everyone ran to the shelter.
After the meeting she walked to the station alone.
Each Sunday the family goes to the market downtown.
The refugees travelled to the border on foot.
He moved to Chicago after finishing school.
We finally got to the hotel around midnight.
The kids raced to the playground after class.
quiet: Last summer my cousins decided to rent a cabin for a week.
When the storm hit, everyone tried to stay calm.
After the meeting she wanted to think alone.
Each Sunday the family likes to cook a big dinner.
The refugees hoped to find work soon.
He planned to study law after finishing school.
We finally managed to sleep around midnight.
The kids begged to play outside after class.

notes: Near misses keep the token ' to' but as an infinitive marker, so the test separates the context from the word.
